items.title: Change records: PR descriptions, commit messages and review replies rendered from a linted machine-readable record
items.description:
Agents write PR descriptions, commit messages and review replies with no template. On the twelve most recent merged PRs every description carried a first-use tracker or criterion id with no gloss, none stated where the change sits in the milestone's tree, none had a risk or blast-radius section, and none listed discovered work; across them there were 46 distinct level-two headings. Commit subjects ran to a median of 91 characters and the repository's squash setting (COMMIT_MESSAGES) concatenates every branch commit's trailers into the merge commit. The owner has to re-read or ask before approving.

This spec decides the three artifact templates (PR body, commit message, review reply), the pipeline that produces them from a JSON change record validated by a schema and linted before anything reaches GitHub, the record's home as an append-only marked PR comment, and a bounded Codex rewrite pass over the record's prose fields. The design inputs are .claude-scratch/git-doc-templates-proposal-v2.md and its mock, and the GPT rewriter brief at docs/reference/2026-10-10-gpt-prose-rewriter-implementation-brief.md.

ADMISSION. Prevents: a PR description the owner cannot read standalone (bare ids, no placement in the milestone tree, no risk or blast radius, discovered work unlisted), a merge commit carrying repeated trailers from the squash setting, and review replies that restate campaign status instead of what changed. All three are observed on PRs 838 to 846. Costs: one shared skill loaded when a PR, commit or reply is written; one PEP 723 script and its suite under content-tests; one PR comment per description revision; one Codex dispatch per rewrite pass; a change to the repository's squash settings. Removed by: twenty consecutive merged PRs pass the record lint with the skill not loaded, or the owner's clarifying questions on PR descriptions stop over that run.

items.title: The change-record spec's errata are amended in one pass and re-attacked once
items.description:
Errata found while implementing the change-record spec (docs/specs/2026-10-10-change-record.md), each implemented to the reading given and awaiting one amendment with one re-attack. (1) Section 2.1 defines the short id as the full id with the prefix removed up to and including the first hyphen, which turns agents-config-9k9.484 into config-9k9.484 against its own example 9k9.484; implemented as the example. (2) CR-L8 and CR-L15 conflict for an init stub, which holds no stamped generated group; implemented as: an absent generated group passes lint, a present one must carry a matching stamp. (3) Section 5's table has no attribution field and no field for a spec PR's blast radius; the schema added commit.attribution. (4) The section 3.1 template says ancestry lines carry a role, CR-X1 says type. (5) Section 2.1's owning item for a direct child of the milestone would be the milestone, and the design mock treats the work item as its own owning item. (6) CR-C1 asks for rounds as a range, but rounds restart per claim and class. (7) CR-L13 has a Deferred reply name the work item the campaign's disposition carries, and real advisory-deferred dispositions carry none. (8) Section 3.4 applies the no-commentary check to four sections, CR-L7 to every author-written prose field; implemented as CR-L7. (9) CR-L7's code-span clause names only the phrase, while CR-C2 relies on a construct in a code span passing; both implemented. (10) CR-L4 as worded passes a verification group with gates and an empty not-run list, though the template always shows a not-run line. (11) CR-L11 names two lists and the None. convention covers three. (12) pr.title and commit.trivial appear in no template, so they have no gloss scope. (13) CR-R1 bounds the text above the horizontal rule at 400 words, and the PR 843 example and the design mock both hold about 1,268 (about 991 outside folds); the check clause never names the count. Vet: the amended spec, a fresh criteria attack record against it, spec-lint exit 0.

## Triage
- Scope: out-of-scope — Each erratum is implemented to the spec's evident intent in the slice that reads it; amending the text invalidates the attack record, so it is one batched amendment, not seven.
- Priority: P3 — No slice is blocked: each implementation follows the spec's own example or criterion and records its reading in a PR body.
- Anchor: agents-config-9k9.484 — The errata are in the spec this container owns, and an amendment needs that spec's criteria re-attacked.

Errata added by the renderer slice, 2026-10-11. (14) Section 3.1's illustration puts the terminal-clean sentence directly under the reviewer table, which GitHub parses as a table row; the template carries a blank line there. (15) Section 3.1 gives an in-flight discovered row no place for its pull request, though CR-L5 requires one; rendered as 'in flight (#n)'. (16) CR-D7 says the author chooses Superseded in the record and does not say how the findings table learns it; read from the matching reply. (17) CR-R4 says 'commit prose fields' without listing them; implemented over every field the commit template names. (18) CR-R6 says 'with the lint output' and names no stream; implemented as stderr. (19) CR-L17 says 'heading' for all three templates, and the commit and reply templates hold labels, not headings.
Erratum added by slice L part c, 2026-10-11. (20) Section 3.3 puts one reply on each finding that changed code or prose, but a finding the reviewing App posts only inside the verdict envelope, with no inline comment, has no thread to reply on. PR 843 has five such fixed findings; the author's account of each fix exists only as the next envelope's prior-disposition evidence. The spec should say where such a reply goes, or that the record entry alone satisfies CR-L14.
Errata added by slice L part c, 2026-10-11. (21) CR-C2 writes a finding's claim and class only when the PR carries more than one, while CR-D7's identity and CR-L14's matching need both always; the schema now requires both on every campaign finding. (22) CR-D7 takes a finding's fix commit from the author's thread reply, so a fixed finding with no thread keeps an empty campaign commit while the record's reply entry holds it. (23) CR-L10 fails a record whose reach flag is true without both diagrams, but a docs or chore body has no blast-radius fold to render them in. (24) CR-L10's 'top-level component' is undefined; implemented as the first path segment, a root file as its own component, and paths under a top-level docs directory counting toward none. (25) CR-L13 does not say which words of a reply count; implemented as the change and verification text, not the labels, outcome or commit. (26) CR-L8's 'exactly the fields the author must fill' cannot hold for the reach flag, which has no unfilled state; the stub sets it false. (27) CR-L3 lists no rule for a subject with no colon or no wording, so such a subject passes.
Errata added by slice C, 2026-10-11. (28) CR-C5, CR-D7 and section 2.1 have the script call the review-verdict skill's completeness rule, but that rule exists only as prose: five checks 'a person checks by hand'. validate_verdict.py holds a validator and no completeness function. Slice C ships without the terminal sha until the owner rules on the function's shape. (29) CR-C5's 'latest envelope' is unsafe on a mixed target: on PR 843 the latest envelope is the prose class's round at the final head, while the code class's last clean round judged an earlier head. (30) A superseded claim's findings never receive a disposition, so a reviewer row's counts do not sum; the spec does not say how a row shows them. (31) CR-C3 does not say which reviews count as envelopes the tool could not read; implemented as App reviews whose envelope block fails to parse or validate. (32) CR-C1's rounds 'as a range' can imply a round a reviewer skipped; the design mock lists rounds one by one.
